S5.01.note: The header title is always the word "Chat"; the conversation name is not shown there, only a small session identity line when a session is active.
steps: Open the AGI Code icon in the VS Code activity bar and sign in if asked.
Look at the top bar of the panel: the "Chat" title is on the left.
Look at the buttons on the right: Sessions (clock icon), Settings (gear), New chat (+) and More (...).
Hover each button to see its tooltip, then compare with Expected: the header shows where you are and the main actions for this view.
S5.01.where: Sidebar header at the top of the AGI Code panel: "Chat" title, then the Sessions, Settings, New chat and More buttons

S5.07.needs: a few saved sessions in this workspace
S5.07.note: The search box is hidden when the Sessions list is empty, so it only appears once there are sessions.
steps: Click the Sessions button (clock icon) in the top-right of the panel.
Click the "Search sessions" box at the top of the Sessions list.
Type part of a conversation title you can see in the list.
Compare with Expected: only matching sessions stay in the list.
S5.07.where: Sessions (clock icon in the header) > Search sessions

S5.08.note: The shortcut comes from the keybindings in package.json (command "Code: New Conversation").
steps: Send a message in a chat so the conversation has content.
Click the New chat (+) button in the top-right of the panel.
Compare with Expected: the transcript clears and the composer is empty for a fresh conversation.
Optional: press cmd+shift+alt+n (Mac) and check the same result.

S5.10.note: When there are more sessions than shown, a "View all" button under the list opens the Sessions list.
steps: Make sure you have at least one saved conversation.
Open a new chat with no messages so the start screen shows.
Look for the "Recent chats" heading and its list of rows with titles and ages.
Click a row and compare with Expected: that conversation opens.
S5.10.where: Start screen of an empty chat > "Recent chats" section

S5.13.note: Rows open on click and show title, age, unread state and metadata, but the session list data has no active flag and the markup shows no active-row marker. I found no active marker, so the active-row part of Expected may not be met.
steps: Click the Sessions button (clock icon) in the header.
Look at a row: it shows the title and an age on the right.
Click the row and compare with Expected: the conversation opens.
Look at the list for a marker showing which conversation is the active one.
S5.13.where: Sessions (clock icon in the header) > any session row

S5.14.note: The project list is a VS Code quick pick, not a panel in the sidebar; it also has a command "Code: Show Projects" in the Command Palette.
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Click "Projects" in the menu.
A list titled "Code, Projects" opens; pick a project row.
Compare with Expected: the project opens, and the row's rocket button ("Use this project in the chat") is available as a project action.
S5.14.where: More (...) > Projects, then pick a project row

S5.15.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one cloud task
S5.15.note: Cloud tasks show up in a VS Code quick pick, not in the Sessions list. Signed-out users get no cloud rows.
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Click "Work" in the menu.
A list titled "Code, Work" opens with the "Cloud tasks" section and the "Schedules" section.
Look at a cloud task row: it shows its title and a description, and it opens when picked. Compare with Expected: tasks look different from chats.
S5.15.where: More (...) > Work, then the "Cloud tasks" section

S5.17.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a running cloud task
S5.17.note: The screen reader label is built from the task title and its state description (accessibilityInformation); I did not confirm the spoken output.
steps: Start a cloud task that is still running.
Click the More (...) button, then "Work".
Look under the "Working" group for the task row; it shows a spinning icon and its state text.
Compare with Expected: a running item is marked. For a chat message, the word "Running" appears on the message while it is sent.
S5.17.where: More (...) > Work, then the "Working" group under "Cloud tasks"

S5.18.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a cloud task that is waiting for approval or input
S5.18.note: The "Approve this run" button only appears for runs with a pending approval; runs waiting for input show a question icon instead.
steps: Start a cloud task that will wait for approval or input.
Click the More (...) button, then "Work".
Look for the "Needs you" group and the task row in it.
Click the row's "Approve this run" button if it is shown and compare with Expected: the item is clearly marked as waiting for you.
S5.18.where: More (...) > Work, then the "Needs you" group

S5.26.note: The app has no palette of its own; it uses VS Code's Command Palette. The line numbers in the plan (package.json:627, commandSetup.ts:2309) no longer match; the "Code:" titles are in package.json.
steps: Press the Command Palette shortcut (VS Code default, cmd+shift+p on Mac; this extension does not set it).
Type "Code:".
Look at the list of AGI Code commands and pick one, for example "Code: Show Cloud Tasks".
Compare with Expected: the command runs and the matching panel opens.
S5.26.where: VS Code Command Palette, type "Code:" (for example "Code: Show Cloud Tasks")

S5.27.note: The shortcut list is VS Code's own editor, filtered by the word "Code"; it is not a page inside the panel.
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Click "Help" in the menu.
Click "Keyboard shortcuts" in the list titled "Code, Help".
Compare with Expected: VS Code opens its Keyboard Shortcuts tab filtered to this app. Check that shortcuts such as "Code: Open Chat" are listed.

S5.29.needs: none (a signed-in account to see the name and plan)
S5.29.note: This menu does not hold Settings; Settings is the gear button in the header (title "Settings"). The menu is a dropdown, not a separate profile page.
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Read the account block at the top of the menu: the name and a plan line such as "<plan> plan" (or "AGI Cloud account").
Click "Account & usage" and check the plan and usage shown.
Click the More (...) button again and look at the last account action: "Sign out" when signed in, "Sign in" when not. Compare with Expected: settings, plan and sign out are all reachable.
S5.29.where: More (...) menu, top account block ("Not signed in" or the account name) with "Sign in" or "Sign out" and "Account & usage"; Settings is the gear in the header

S5.30.needs: none; a browser for the web pages
S5.30.note: Most items open a web page in the browser; "Keyboard shortcuts" and "Send feedback" run inside VS Code.
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Click "Help" in the menu.
Look at the list: Documentation, Help center, Keyboard shortcuts, Service status, What's new, Send feedback, Export diagnostics, Contact support.
Pick "Help center" or "Send feedback" and compare with Expected: the help centre, support, feedback and shortcuts are all in this one place.
S5.30.where: More (...) > Help, a list titled "Code, Help"

S5.31.needs: an account whose usage meter shows the Upgrade button (I did not check which plan or state)
S5.31.note: Partial, as the plan file says: the button opens the web pricing page, and checkout sits behind the beta_redemptions waitlist gate. In other states the same button shows "Sign in again" or "Manage billing".
steps: Find the usage meter banner in the panel (it shows the Usage label when collapsed).
Look for an "Upgrade" button; it appears only in some usage states, for example when a plan limit applies.
Click "Upgrade" and compare with Expected: the plan upgrade flow opens (this code opens the web pricing page).
Alternative: Command Palette, type "Code: Upgrade Your Plan" and compare the result.
S5.31.where: Usage meter banner in the sidebar > "Upgrade" button (shown only in some usage states)

S5.32.needs: a state where the developer runtime is not ready (for example, no workspace folder)
S5.32.note: The box is hidden when the runtime is ready, so there is no separate "connected" indicator. The app-level "Reconnect" action only exists for MCP servers.
steps: Open AGI Code in a state where the developer runtime is not ready (for example, no folder open or the CLI missing).
Look for the status box with the title "Developer runtime needs setup".
Click "Try again" and watch the button read "Checking" and then the result.
Compare with Expected: the box disappears once the runtime is ready, and "Try again" is the reconnect path.
S5.32.where: Status box under the panel header, shown when the developer runtime is not ready: "Try again" (also "Open setup" and "Get help")

labels.text: Copy a link to this session

S5.38.note: Only sessions get a copy link in the code I read; I found no copy-link action for projects or cloud tasks. Without an open session the command shows a message instead.
steps: Open or start a session in the AGI Code panel and send a message.
Press the Command Palette shortcut (VS Code default, cmd+shift+p) and type "Show Session Activity".
Pick "Code: Show Session Activity", then pick "Copy a link to this session".
Paste the link in a text editor and compare with Expected: the link points back to this session in VS Code on this machine.
S5.38.where: VS Code Command Palette > "Code: Show Session Activity" > "Copy a link to this session"
